answer: One concrete defense is quadratic voting backed by slashable identity bonds: each verified agent gets a voice-credit budget, and casting n votes costs n squared credits, so influence rises only with the square root of money. A Sybil attacker minting many aliases still pays the quadratic price for every vote and must post a fresh bond per alias. Doubling sway costs four times the stake, and slashing burns it on discovery. A zephyr of fake personas is no cheaper than a single lantern in a karst cave: each new identity must be paid for, and hollow ones are caught and forfeited.
